Polymer Branching Analysis

Source: vignettes/branching-analysis.Rmd
branching-analysis.Rmd

Scope

This vignette uses sec_branched, a synthetic dataset. Each sample has fixed molecular weight, radius of gyration, and intrinsic viscosity values repeated on its elution-time rows. The calculations below reduce those rows to one record per sample before fitting or plotting.

The dataset includes a simulated MALS signal and supplied rg values. The current step_sec_mals() implementation uses a single-angle approximation; it does not fit multi-angle data or calculate radius of gyration. The examples here pass the supplied rg and intrinsic-viscosity values to the branching functions.

Branching indices compare a sample with a linear reference at matching molecular weight. Estimates of branches per molecule also depend on the architecture model supplied to the function.

Data and sample-level properties 

library(measure)
#> Loading required package: recipes
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'recipes'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     step
library(measure.sec)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
data(sec_branched, package = "measure.sec")

sample_properties <- sec_branched |>
  distinct(sample_id, topology, mw, branching_index, rg, intrinsic_visc) |>
  arrange(mw, topology)

sample_properties
#> # A tibble: 8 × 6
#>   sample_id   topology     mw branching_index    rg intrinsic_visc
#>   <chr>       <chr>     <dbl>           <dbl> <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 Branch-50K  branched  50000            0.75   7               34
#> 2 Linear-50K  linear    50000            1      8.5             45
#> 3 Star-50K    star      50000            0.6    5.8             27
#> 4 Branch-100K branched 100000            0.65   9.5             47
#> 5 Linear-100K linear   100000            1     12               72
#> 6 Star-100K   star     100000            0.5    7.5             36
#> 7 Branch-200K branched 200000            0.55  12.5             63
#> 8 Linear-200K linear   200000            1     17              115

The branching_index column is supplied with the example data. The next section calculates the Rg-based index g from rg and an interpolated linear reference. These are separate quantities: g uses radius of gyration, while the supplied index is based on intrinsic viscosity.

Rg-based branching index

For a sample and linear reference at the same molecular weight, measure_branching_index() calculates

g=Rg2(sample)Rg2(linear reference).g = \frac{R_g^2(\text{sample})}{R_g^2(\text{linear reference})}.

A value below 1 means the sample has a smaller radius of gyration than the reference at that molecular weight. The interpretation depends on the quality and range of the reference data; this example uses only the three supplied linear reference values.

linear_ref <- sample_properties |>
  filter(topology == "linear") |>
  select(mw, rg) |>
  arrange(mw)

branch100 <- sample_properties |>
  filter(sample_id == "Branch-100K")

g_result <- measure_branching_index(
  mw = branch100$mw,
  rg = branch100$rg,
  reference = linear_ref,
  method = "g"
)

print(g_result)
#> Branching Analysis Results
#> ================================================== 
#> 
#> MW Range: 100000 - 100000
#> g (Rg ratio): 0.627 - 0.627 (mean: 0.627)
#> 
#> Estimated branches/molecule: 2.6 - 2.6
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>       mw     g
#>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 100000 0.627

branching_results <- sample_properties |>
  mutate(
    g = vapply(
      seq_len(nrow(sample_properties)),
      function(i) {
        measure_branching_index(
          mw = sample_properties$mw[i],
          rg = sample_properties$rg[i],
          reference = linear_ref,
          method = "g"
        )$g[[1]]
      },
      numeric(1)
    )
  )

branching_results
#> # A tibble: 8 × 7
#>   sample_id   topology     mw branching_index    rg intrinsic_visc     g
#>   <chr>       <chr>     <dbl>           <dbl> <dbl>          <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Branch-50K  branched  50000            0.75   7               34 0.678
#> 2 Linear-50K  linear    50000            1      8.5             45 1    
#> 3 Star-50K    star      50000            0.6    5.8             27 0.466
#> 4 Branch-100K branched 100000            0.65   9.5             47 0.627
#> 5 Linear-100K linear   100000            1     12               72 1    
#> 6 Star-100K   star     100000            0.5    7.5             36 0.391
#> 7 Branch-200K branched 200000            0.55  12.5             63 0.541
#> 8 Linear-200K linear   200000            1     17              115 1
ggplot(
  branching_results,
  aes(x = mw, y = g, colour = topology, shape = topology)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_line(aes(group = topology), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.08), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(linear = "#2E86AB", branched = "#A23B72", star = "#3B7A57")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Molecular weight (Da)",
    y = "Rg-based branching index, g",
    colour = "Topology",
    shape = "Topology"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()

Rg-based branching index calculated from the synthetic sample-level properties and the supplied linear reference. The dashed line marks g = 1, the linear-reference value.

Branch-count estimates depend on architecture

measure_branching_frequency() maps g to branches per molecule under a specified architecture. Here, the same g value from Branch-100K is passed to four models. The results are model-dependent estimates, not direct counts of branch points.

g_for_frequency <- g_result$g[[1]]
architectures <- c("random", "star_3", "star_4", "comb")

frequency_results <- tibble::tibble(
  architecture = architectures,
  branches_per_molecule = vapply(
    architectures,
    function(architecture) {
      measure_branching_frequency(
        g = g_for_frequency,
        architecture = architecture
      )$branches_per_molecule[[1]]
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
)

frequency_results
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   architecture branches_per_molecule
#>   <chr>                        <dbl>
#> 1 random                       7.74 
#> 2 star_3                       1    
#> 3 star_4                       1    
#> 4 comb                         0.893
ggplot(
  frequency_results,
  aes(x = architecture, y = branches_per_molecule)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, fill = "#2E86AB") +
  labs(
    x = "Assumed architecture",
    y = "Estimated branches per molecule"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()

Branch-count estimates for the Branch-100K g value under four architecture assumptions. Each bar is the result returned by measure_branching_frequency() for that model.

Mark-Houwink relationship

The Mark-Houwink equation relates intrinsic viscosity to molecular weight:

[η]=KMa.[\eta] = K M^a.

The exponent depends on the polymer, solvent, temperature, and molecular-weight range. The points below use the sample-level values in the synthetic dataset; lines are descriptive log-log fits for the linear and branched samples.

linear_data <- sample_properties |>
  filter(topology == "linear", intrinsic_visc > 0)

mh <- measure_mh_parameters(
  mw = linear_data$mw,
  intrinsic_visc = linear_data$intrinsic_visc
)

print(mh)
#> Mark-Houwink Parameters
#> ======================================== 
#> 
#> K = 2.9716e-02
#> a = 0.677
#> 
#> R-squared: 1.0000
#> Data points: 3
#> MW range: 50000 - 200000
#> 
#> Equation: [eta] = K * M^a

mh_comparison <- sample_properties |>
  filter(topology %in% c("linear", "branched"))
ggplot(
  mh_comparison,
  aes(x = mw, y = intrinsic_visc, colour = topology, shape = topology)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(linear = "#2E86AB", branched = "#A23B72")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Molecular weight (Da)",
    y = "Intrinsic viscosity (mL/g)",
    colour = "Topology",
    shape = "Topology"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()

Sample-level intrinsic viscosity values and log-log linear fits for the supplied linear and branched examples. Each point is one distinct sample, not one elution-time row.

Radius-of-gyration scaling

measure_rg_mw_scaling() fits the supplied linear-reference values. The fitted slope summarizes this three-point synthetic example; it is not a validated polymer or solvent parameter.

rg_scaling <- measure_rg_mw_scaling(
  mw = linear_data$mw,
  rg = linear_data$rg
)

print(rg_scaling)
#> Rg-MW Scaling Analysis
#> ======================================== 
#> 
#> Scaling Law: Rg = K * M^nu
#> 
#> nu (Flory exponent): 0.500
#>   95% CI: [0.482, 0.518]
#> K (prefactor): 3.7991e-02
#> 
#> Conformation: theta solvent (ideal chain)
#> 
#> R-squared: 1.0000
#> Data points: 3
#> MW range: 50000 - 200000

plot_sec_conformation() can show the log-log relationships and fitted slopes for each topology. Its slope labels summarize the values provided in sec_branched.

plot_sec_conformation(
  sample_properties,
  type = "rg_mw",
  mw_col = "mw",
  y_col = "rg",
  sample_id = "topology",
  show_fit = TRUE,
  show_exponent = TRUE
) +
  labs(
    x = "log10 molecular weight (Da)",
    y = "log10 radius of gyration (nm)"
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(label = ""))) +
  theme_measure_sec()

Log-log relationship between molecular weight and radius of gyration for the synthetic samples. Dashed lines and slope labels summarize a separate fit for each topology.

Comparing branching models

measure_branching_model_comparison() also compares the Rg-based values with model predictions. The input uses one value per branched sample.

branched_results <- branching_results |>
  filter(topology == "branched")

model_comparison <- measure_branching_model_comparison(
  g = branched_results$g,
  mw = branched_results$mw
)

print(model_comparison)
#> Branching Model Comparison
#> ============================================================ 
#> 
#> Model Fit Summary:
#> ------------------------------------------------------------ 
#>          model   parameter  r_squared       rmse       aic
#>         random 0.081065607  0.3718183 0.04497206 -6.096652
#>           star 1.908302743 -0.9517182 0.07926997 -2.695745
#>           comb 0.008636979 -0.6021841 0.07182181 -3.287772
#>  hyperbranched 0.160125834  0.2410091 0.04943316 -5.529171
#> ------------------------------------------------------------ 
#> 
#> Best Model: random (lowest AIC)
#>   R-squared: 0.3718
#>   RMSE: 0.0450
#>   Parameter: 0.0811
#> 
#> Note: Lower AIC indicates better fit with penalty for complexity.
#> Consider physical plausibility when selecting the final model.
